stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist is subject to two separate events: another state's board disciplines her nursing licence, and a week later she is criminally charged in Massachusetts. Which reporting statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Neither event is reportable until the criminal matter reaches a final disposition.
The out-of-state final action against her other health care licence must be reported within seven business days.
The out-of-state action is reportable only if it involved the practice of pharmacy.
The pending criminal charge must be reported to the Board in writing within 30 days.
Both events share a single 30-day reporting deadline.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.03(1)(z) makes it a ground for discipline to fail to report within seven business days any final action by another governmental authority regarding a registrant, including action against any other health care related registration the person holds. 247 CMR 10.03(1)(aa) separately requires written report of any pending criminal charge or conviction within 30 days. The two clocks are different and run from different triggers.

choice_analysis.A: The charge duty is triggered by the charge pending, not by final disposition.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: seven business days, and the duty expressly reaches other health care credentials.
choice_analysis.C: The duty covers action against any other health care related registration or licence.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: 30 days in writing, triggered while the charge is merely pending.
choice_analysis.E: The deadlines differ: seven business days and 30 days.

related_facts: Failing to report accurately is a ground for discipline alongside failing to report at all.
explanation.mpje_trap: Two clocks run from two triggers, and one is measured in business days while the other is not.

reasoning_steps: Classify each event against the two separate reporting grounds
Apply the seven-business-day clock to the out-of-state final action
Apply the 30-day written clock to the pending criminal charge
